chunks: 1743 - Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a beggar who asks, while it is not known what his condition is, so he said:
"Give to the one for whom mercy falls into your heart." And he said: "Give him less than a dirham."
I said: "What is the most that may be given?" He said: "Four daniqs."

key_terms.أَعْطِهِ: give to him; an instruction to offer charity
key_terms.دَوَانِيقَ: daniqs; smaller monetary units, here specifying the upper amount mentioned
key_terms.ٱلدِّرْهَمِ: a dirham; a standard unit of money used as a measure for giving
key_terms.ٱلرَّحْمَةُ: mercy or compassion felt toward the petitioner
key_terms.ٱلسَّائِلِ: the one who asks; a beggar or petitioner seeking charity

ai.seo_question: How much should be given to a beggar whose condition is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses giving charity to a petitioner whose real condition is unknown. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام directs the giver to respond to sincere compassion in the heart, while also indicating a measured amount for such giving. It combines moral sensitivity with practical guidance in charity.
